Output 0 of the decoder is connected to the DS1 select terminal of the I/O device. The data outputs D0-D7 of the I/O device on the right are connected to the data bus D0-D7 of the 8085. At the lower right of the figure there is also a set of gate circuitry in which A8, A9, A10 pass through inverters and A11, A12, A13, A14, A15 directly participate, and its output is connected to the DS2 select terminal of the I/O device. Reasoning: When the left decoder is to select output 0, A2 A1 A0 must be 000; at the same time, A3-A7 form a valid selection through gate circuitry, requiring A3=A4=A5=A6=A7=1. Therefore the lower 8-bit address A7...A0 = 11111000₂ = F8H. In the right-side gate circuitry, A8, A9, A10 are first inverted before entering the gate circuitry, so they should be 0; A11-A15 enter the gate circuitry directly, so they should be 1. Therefore the upper 8-bit address A15...A8 = 11111000₂ = F8H. This peripheral is therefore memory-mapped to address F8F8H. For the 8085 to read a memory-mapped input device into the accumulator, the LDA addr instruction should be used, so the correct instruction is LDA F8F8H.
